chapter_name: Liberalisation, Privatisation and Globalisation: An Appraisal
learning_objective: 🎯 Understand the severe 1991 economic crisis and the subsequent LPG reforms that opened up the Indian economy to the world.

key_vocabulary.definition: A severe Balance of Payments crisis where India barely had enough foreign exchange reserves to cover two weeks of imports.
Removing government restrictions, controls, and licenses to allow private businesses to operate freely.
Transferring the ownership, management, or control of public sector enterprises to the private sector.
Integrating the national economy with the global economy by removing barriers to international trade and investment.
Hiring external agencies (often in other countries like India) to perform business processes like customer support or IT.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: By 1991, massive government spending led to high inflation and a Balance of Payments crisis. India approached the World Bank and IMF for a $7 billion loan. The IMF agreed, but strictly conditioned it on India opening up its economy. This led to the New Economic Policy (NEP) of 1991.

The 'License Raj' was dismantled. Industrial licensing was abolished for most sectors. Financial sectors were deregulated, allowing private banks. Foreign exchange was deregulated by devaluing the Rupee, and import tariffs were drastically reduced.

The government started selling its shares in Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) to the private sector and the public. This process is called 'Disinvestment'. The goal was to improve efficiency, discipline, and modernize management.

India integrated with the world. Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) flooded in. Thanks to a large, English-speaking, skilled workforce, India became a global hub for BPO (Business Process Outsourcing) and IT services.

fun_activity.title: 🎧 The Call Center Revolution
fun_activity.instructions: Why do companies in the US and UK route their customer care calls to India? It's simple Economics! A worker in the US might charge $15 an hour. An equally skilled English-speaking worker in India might charge $3 an hour. Globalisation allowed this 'Outsourcing', creating millions of IT/BPO jobs in India!

exam_tips: 📌 Always distinguish between Stabilisation measures (short-term fixes like controlling inflation/BoP) and Structural reforms (long-term fixes like LPG to improve efficiency).
📌 A critical failure of the LPG reforms is that while the Services sector boomed, the Agriculture sector (which employs the most people) was largely neglected and its growth rate declined.
📌 Devaluation of the Rupee in 1991 made Indian exports cheaper and more competitive in the international market, helping solve the forex crisis.
quick_recap: ⭐ The New Economic Policy (NEP) was introduced under the leadership of Finance Minister Dr. Manmohan Singh.
⭐ Liberalisation ended the monopoly of the public sector in areas like telecommunications, aviation, and banking.
⭐ The WTO was founded in 1995 as the successor to GATT to establish rule-based trading regimes globally.
